questions.prompt:
What number comes next in this pattern?
81, 72, 63, 54, ___
questions.hint: How much is taken away each time?
questions.solution: The pattern takes away 9 each time. 54 − 9 = 45.

questions.prompt: A rectangle is 8 cm long and 5 cm wide. What is its area?
questions.hint: Area of a rectangle = length × width.

questions.prompt: Today is Friday. What day of the week was it 3 days ago?
questions.hint: Count backwards one day at a time.
questions.solution: 1 day ago: Thursday. 2 days ago: Wednesday. 3 days ago: Tuesday.

questions.prompt: How many tens are in 3,450?
questions.hint: Think of 3,450 as a stack of ten-dollar bills.

questions.prompt: A movie ended at 4:10 PM. It was 95 minutes long. At what time did the movie start?
questions.hint: 95 minutes is 1 hour and 35 minutes. Count backwards.
questions.solution: 95 minutes = 1 hour 35 minutes. 4:10 PM − 1 hour = 3:10 PM. 3:10 PM − 35 minutes = 2:35 PM.

questions.prompt: A pumpkin and a gourd cost $11 together. The pumpkin costs $5 more than the gourd. How much does the pumpkin cost?
questions.hint: If the pumpkin cost the same as the gourd, how much would they cost together?
questions.solution: Take away the extra $5: 11 − 5 = $6 for two gourd-sized prices, so the gourd costs $3. The pumpkin costs 3 + 5 = $8.

questions.prompt: There are 3 roads from Town A to Town B and 4 roads from Town B to Town C. How many different ways can you drive from Town A to Town C, going through Town B?
questions.hint: Each road from A to B can be followed by any road from B to C.
questions.solution: 3 choices for the first part × 4 choices for the second part = 12 ways.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest 4-digit number whose digits are all different?
questions.hint: The first digit can't be 0. Make every digit as small as you can, from left to right.
questions.solution: The thousands digit must be at least 1. Then use 0, 2 and 3 for the other places: 1,023.

questions.prompt: Jin makes the frame of a cube out of wire. Each edge of the cube is 5 cm long. How many centimeters of wire does he use?
questions.hint: How many edges does a cube have?
questions.solution: A cube has 12 edges: 4 on top, 4 on the bottom and 4 going up the sides. 12 × 5 = 60 cm.

questions.prompt:
What number goes in the box?
3 × □ + 8 = 50
questions.hint: First find what 3 × □ must be.

questions.prompt: Noah's scores on four spelling tests were 85, 90, 75 and 90. What was his average (mean) score?
questions.hint: Add the scores, then divide by the number of tests.

questions.prompt: A class has 45 students. Two-thirds of them walk to school. How many students walk to school?
questions.hint: First find one-third of 45.
questions.solution: One-third of 45 is 45 ÷ 3 = 15. Two-thirds is 2 × 15 = 30 students.

questions.prompt: How many rectangles of any size are in this strip of 4 squares? (Squares count as rectangles too.)
questions.hint: Count rectangles that are 1 square long, then 2 squares long, then 3, then 4.
questions.solution: 1 square long: 4. 2 long: 3. 3 long: 2. 4 long: 1. Total: 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.

questions.prompt: There are 20 kids in a club. Every kid likes soccer or basketball or both. 13 kids like soccer and 11 kids like basketball. How many kids like both?
questions.hint: 13 + 11 counts some kids twice.
questions.solution: 13 + 11 = 24, but there are only 20 kids. The kids who like both were counted twice, so 24 − 20 = 4 kids like both.

questions.prompt: Spiders have 8 legs and beetles have 6 legs. A science box holds 10 bugs with 68 legs in all. How many spiders are in the box?
questions.hint: Pretend all 10 bugs are beetles. How many legs would that be?
questions.solution: 10 beetles would have 60 legs. There are 68 − 60 = 8 extra legs. Each spider has 2 more legs than a beetle, so 8 ÷ 2 = 4 spiders.

questions.prompt: How many 2-digit numbers have a tens digit that is greater than the ones digit? (For example, 31 counts but 13 and 33 do not.)
questions.hint: If the tens digit is 1, the ones digit can only be 0. If the tens digit is 2, how many choices?
questions.solution: Tens digit 1: 1 number (10). Tens digit 2: 2 numbers (20, 21). … Tens digit 9: 9 numbers. 1 + 2 + 3 + … + 9 = 45.

questions.prompt: A big square is cut into 4 equal smaller squares, 2 across and 2 down. The perimeter of one small square is 20 cm. What is the perimeter of the big square?
questions.hint: First find the side of a small square.
questions.solution: Small square side: 20 ÷ 4 = 5 cm. The big square's side is 2 small sides: 10 cm. Big perimeter: 4 × 10 = 40 cm.

questions.prompt: A hallway has 10 closed lockers numbered 1 to 10. Student 1 opens every locker. Student 2 changes every 2nd locker (opens it if closed, closes it if open). Student 3 changes every 3rd locker, and so on, until Student 10 changes locker 10. How many lockers are open at the end?
questions.hint: A locker ends up open if it is changed an odd number of times. How many factors does each locker number have?
questions.solution: Locker n is changed once for each factor of n. Only numbers with an odd number of factors stay open: 1, 4 and 9 (they are square numbers). So 3 lockers are open.

questions.prompt: The sum of two numbers is 50. Their difference is 14. What is the product of the two numbers?
questions.hint: Find the two numbers first. Take away the difference, then split the rest in half.
questions.solution: 50 − 14 = 36, and half of 36 is 18, the smaller number. The larger is 18 + 14 = 32. Product: 32 × 18 = 576.
